IS : 994 - 1964

Indian

Standard

SPECIFICATION FOR BUTTER KNIVES AND FISH KNIVES ( Revised )
0.
FOREWORD

0.1 This revised Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 June 1964, after the draft finalized by the Cutlery Sectional Committee had been approved by the Consumer Products Division Council. 0.2 This standard was first published in 1957 and was one of a series of Indian Standard specifications on table cutlery. Revision of the series has been taken up on account of the necessity to metricize and also to avoid such details as will hinder the improvement of design. Other standards in the series are: IS :990-1964 SPOONS, STAINLESSSTEEL ( Revised) IS :99 l- 1964 SPOONS, BRASS AND NICKEL SILVER ( Revised) IS:992-l964 FORKS (TABLE, FISH, PASTRY AND SERVING),STAINLESSSTEEL ( Revised)
IS:

993-1964 FORKS (TABLE, FISH, PASTRY AND SERVING), BRASS AND NICKEL SILVER ( Revised)

IS :995-1964 TABLE KNIVES, DESSEFU KNIVES AND FRUIT KNIVES ( Revised )
0.3

This standard deals with the requirements for butter knives and fish knives. Designs other than those covered by this standard are also popular with certain organizations to suit aesthetic requirements. In such cases, it is recommended that the knives may be made according to the designs of the individual organizations but other provisions of the standard shall apply to guide the manufacture and purchase. An important aspect of table cutlery is that the different items in a set such as spoons, forks and knives should match in, shape and appearance. This fact is to be borne in mind by the manufacturers when supplying cutlery in sets.

0.4 Wherever a reference to any Indian Standard appears in this specification, it shall be taken as a reference to the latest version of the standard. 3

IS:!KH-1964 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of; a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960 Rules for Rounding Off Numerical Values ( Rerised ) . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should ,be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 0.6 This standard is intended chiefly to cover the technical provisions relating to butter knives and fish knives, and it does not include all the necessary provisions of a contract.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This knives: standard covers the requirements for the following types of

a) Butter knives ( see Fig. 1 ), and b) Fish knives of stainless steel or `nickel silver ( see Fig. 2 ) with: 1) stainless steel or nickel silver solid handle forged with blade, or 2) stainless steel or nickel silver hollow handle, or 3) plastics handle. 2. MATERIAL 2.0 The butter knives and fish knives shall be made either of stainless steel or nickel silver. 2.1 The stainless steel used for the manufacture of butter knives and fish knives shall conform to designation 07Cr19Ni9 of Schedule V of IS : 15701961 Schedules for Wrought Steels for General Engineering Purposes. 2.2 Nickel silver used in the manufacture of butter knives and fish knives shall conform to Grade NSlO or NS20 as specified in IS : 2283-1962 Specification for Nickel Silver Sheet and Strip for General Purposes. 2.3 Plastics Handles -The plastics material shall be free from It deleterious substances and shall resist the action of dilute organic-acids. shall not be so inflammable as to burst into flames when a lighted match is applied to it. 3. SHAPES AND DIMENSIONS 3.1 Butter knives and fish knives shall conform to the shapes and dimensions given in Fig. 1 and 2, respectively. 4

All dimensions in milliietres. Fm. 2

FISH KNIFE

3.1.1 Knives may also have shapes and dimensions other than those given in the standard subject to agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser. The knives shall, however, conform with the other provisions laid down in this standard. 3.2 The design of the handles of knives shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer and the purchaser. When spoons, forks and knives are required to be supplied in sets, the design of the handles and general appearance of the items in a set shall match. 4. MANUFACTURE 4.1 Fish knives with solid handles and butter knives shall be forged in one piece. 5

4.2 Fish knives with hollow handles shall have the blades forged and the taligs well drawn. The scales shall fit closely to the tang and shall be finished flush and smooth. The joints shall be silver-soldered in case of nickel silver hollow handles and welded in case' of stainless steel hollow handles. 4.3 Where the plastics handles are cast, they shall be soundly moulded with the tang in position. The tang shall be properly shaped and grooved. The end of the tang shall be at least 15 mm away from free end. Where plastics handles are fitted, the length of the tang shall be at least 65 mm to ensure rigid fixing. 4.4 The blades shall be properly ground and tapered as shown in Fig. 1 and 2. 5. WORKMANSHIP

AND FINISH

5.1 Workmanship - The knives shall be frtie from cracks, seams, flaws, scales, pits, burrs, rough grind ma&s and other defects. They shall be finished smooth all over and polished bright. All sharp edges and corners except the cutting edge shall be slightly rounded. The blade and the h?ndle shall be in good alignment so that: a) in the case of butter knife, the centre line of the blade and the handle is the same; and b) in the case of fish knife, when placed on a table the knife rests w.ithout the blade touching the surface of the table. 5.2 Finish - Hollow handle fitted to stainless steel fish knives, and butter and fish knives made from NS20 grade nickel silver shall be unplated unless otherwise specified by the purchaser. 5.2:1 Hollow handles fitted to stainless steel fish knives and butter and fish knives made from NS 10 grade niizkel silver shall be in any of the following finishes as may be specified by the purchaser: Finish a) Nickel b) Nickel and chromium c) Silver Minimum Thickness 15 microns Nickel 15 microns, and chromium 0.5 micron 40 microns .

5.2.2 The plating shall conform to IS : 1068-1958 Specification for Copper, Nickel and Chromium Electroplated Coatings, in the case of nickel and chromium platings; and to IS : 1067-1958 Specification for Commercial Silver Plating, in the case of silver plating. 6

ISr!l94-1964 6. DESIGNATION 6.1 The designation of the knife shall indicate: a) name; b) material and, in the case of fish knife, the type of handle; and c) number of this standard. Examjh 1: Butter Knife, Stainless Steel or `SS', IS : 994 Exam@c 2: A stainless steel fish knife with hollow handle made of nickel silver shall be designated as : Stainless Steel Fish Knife, Nickel Silver Hollow Handle,,IS 7. TESTS 7.1 Sampling - The number of knives ascertaining conformity to this specification the manufacturer and the purchaser. A criteria for conformity for knives are given to be selected from `a lot for shall be as agreed to between suitable sampling scheme andin Appendix A. : 994

A butter knife made of stainless steel shall be designated as:

7.2 Staining Test for Stainless Steel Knives and Blades - The knife, when dipped for 16 hours in each of the following solutions, shall not show any sign of staining after removal from the solution at the end of the above period: a) Ten grams of glacial acetic acid ( 99 percent ) dissolved in distilled water to make 100 ml, and b) Five grams of pure sodium chloride dissolved in distilled water to make 100 ml. 7.3 Test for Knives with Hollow Handles - Hollow handles after fitting shall be immersed for 30 seconds in clean air-free water maintained at 80�C. They shall not show any expulsion of air bubbles. 7.4 Tests for Fish Knives with Plastics Handles 7.4.1 Boiling - The knife shall be immersed for one hour in a boiling J-percent soap-solution, then rinsed immediately in water at 15" to 20�C and immediately reimmersed completely in boiling water for one hour. The knife shall then be rinsed again in water at 15" to 20�C. This procedure shall be repeated four times. During or on completion of the test, the 7

IS:994-1964 handle shall not show any sign of cracking, chipping or discolouring of the plastics. The tang shall neither become loose nor shall there be any other damage. 7.4.2 Impact - This test shall be conducted after the boiling test. The knife shall be held with the handle facing downwards and dropped from a height of l-2 m on to a concrete floor or a flat stone five times in succession. The handle shall not show any sign of cracking, breaking or chipping of the plastics and tang shall neither become loose nor shall there be any other damage. plastics handle shall be cut into three pieces and 7.4.3 Staining -The 2ach piece shall be immersed in one of the following solutions, maintained at room temperature: a) Sodium chloride solution, 10 percent ( w/v); b) Acetic acid solution, 5 percent ( v/v); and c) Sodium carbonate solution, 2 percent ( w/v). Each piece shall be taken out after 24 hours, rinsed with tap water and wiped with a dry cloth. It shall then be examined and immersed again in the same solution. This process shall be repeated seven times. During and at the end of seven days' test there shall be no perceptible change in the appearance of the plastics material. 8. MARKING 8.1 Each k.nife shall be legibly and indelibly etched on its blade near the bolster with the following abbreviations and the manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark: Symbol `SS' NS20 NSN NSNC NSS 8.1.1 Material or Finish Stainless steel Nickel silver, Grade NS20 Nickel silver, nickel plated Nickel silver, nickel and chromium plated Nickel silver, silver plated

The knives may also be marked with the IS1 Certification Mark.

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Catification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been producedto complywith the requrrements of that standard under a well-defined system of mspectron,testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. IS1 marked

9. PACKING 9.1 The knives shall be wrapped in soft tissue paper or wax paper and The number of knives to be packed in one carton packed in cartons. shall be at the discretion of the manufacturers. The cartons shall bear the type and number of knives packed, the name of the manufacturer and the country of manufacture.

APPENDIX ( CZause 7.1 )

A

SAMPLING SCHEME AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY FOR BUTTER KNIVES AND FISH KNIVES A-l. SCALE OF SAMPLING

A-l.1 Lot - In any consignment, all the knives of the same type of handle, shape and size, manufactured from the same material under relatively similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. A-l .2 For ascertaining the conformity to the requirements of this speciilcation the tests shall be conducted separately for each lot. A-1.3 The number of knives to be selected from a lot for ascertaining conformity to the requirements of this specification, shall be according to co1 2 of Table I. The knives in the sample shall be selected at random from the lot. If the knives are packed in cartons, as a first step at least 25 percent of the cartons shall be selected at random and then from each selected carton, equal number of knives shall be taken out at random so as to make the requirea sample size. A-2. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

A-2.1 The knives selected at random according to A-l.3 shall be examined A knife failing to satisfy one or more for the requirements of 3.1 and 5.1. of these requirements shall be regarded as defective. The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of 3.1 and 5.1 if the number of defective knives in the sample does not exceed the number given in co1 3 of Table I. 9
